AGENDA
OF A REGULAR MEETING
OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA 90274
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
This meeting will be conducted in a hybrid format, allowing members of the public to attend in person or remotely using the teleconference or videoconference information provided below.
REMOTE MEETING PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
Zoom Meeting Link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84327898806
Meeting ID: 843 2789 8806
Dial-In Number(s): (669) 900-9128
Members of the public may also participate in this meeting at the following location:
The Resort at Kapalua Bay, 1 Bay Drive, Suite 3602, Lahaina, HI 96761
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit email correspondence to CityClerks@pvestates.org before the meeting begins. The email will be
distributed to all councilmembers. Public correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting while participating remotely, please utilize the "Raise Hand" feature during the
meeting, or email CityClerks@pvestates.org with (1) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (2) the phone number and/or Zoom display name from which you will be calling in to the meeting.
Agenda reports and other disclosable public documents relating to each Agenda Item are available on the City's website under City Council Meeting Agendas at www.pvestates.org.

This portion of the agenda is reserved for comments from the public on items which are NOT on the agenda. Due to state law, no action can be taken by the Council this evening on matters presented under this section. If the Council determines action is warranted, the item may be referred to staff or placed on a future Council agenda.
Public Correspondence
CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1 –6)
1.
APPROVAL OF WARRANTS
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve Jul 14, 2026, Warrant Register.
Warrants
2.
CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Minutes of Special and Regular City Council Meetings of June 23, 2026.
Mintutes
3.
ADOPTION OF A PROPOSED RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO RELEASE WARRANTS DURING THE MONTH OF AUGUST 2026
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt proposed Resolution No. R26-24 authorizing the City Manager or designee to release warrants (including payroll and accounts payable) during the month of August 2026.
Staff Report
Attachment 1
4.
RECEIVE AND FILE THE FINAL 2026 CITYWIDE STORM DRAIN MASTER PLAN (SDMP)
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the final 2026 Citywide Storm Drain Master Plan (SDMP), which establishes a comprehensive framework for future storm drain infrastructure investments, asset management, capital improvement planning, and grant funding opportunities.
Staff Report
Attachment A
Attachment B
Attachment C
5.
MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, AND THE FOUR PENINSULA CITIES FOR THE COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING PROGRAM (CIMP)
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve and authorize the City Manager to execute the new Memorandum of Agreement among the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, the County of Los Angeles, and the Cities of Rancho Palos Verdes, Palos Verdes Estates, Rolling Hills, and Rolling Hills Estates regarding administration and cost sharing for implementation of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program (CIMP), and direct staff to notify the participating agencies that the City elects not to participate in Optional Task 8 (Santa Monica Bay Beaches Bacteria TMDL Monitoring).
Staff Report
Attachment A
Attachment B
Attachment C
Attachment D
6.
CERTIFICATION OF THE JUNE 2, 2026, SPECIAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. R26-25 Reciting the Facts of the Special Municipal Election Held on June 2, 2026, Declaring the Results and Such Other Matters as Provided by Law.
Staff Report
Attachment A
NEW BUSINESS
7.
REVIEW OF COMMUNITY SURVEY RESULTS REGARDING FUTURE FUNDING OPTIONS FOLLOWING THE EXPIRATION OF MEASURE E; CONSIDERATION OF POTENTIAL MEASURE E REPLACEMENT OPTIONS; AND DIRECTION REGARDING BALLOT MEASURE STRUCTURE AND REVENUE STRATEGY
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council: 1) Review the results of the community survey regarding a potential replacement for Measure E; 2) Discuss and provide direction regarding the preferred funding level and structure of a potential Measure E replacement measure; 3) Provide direction regarding the inclusion of: inflationary cost escalators, funding for unfunded pension liabilities, restrictions on the use of funds for new facilities or expansion projects, and annual oversight and reporting requirements; and 4) Consider whether a future measure should be limited to public safety funding or other directed priorities.
Staff Report

Attachment 5
